For the Appellant : Mr. Arvind Kumar Choudhary, Advocate For the State : Mr. Shiv Shankar Kumar, A.P.P. For the Informant : Mr. Onkar Nath Tiwary, Advocate ---
04/08.05.2025 I.A. No. 5381 of 2025 Mr. Shiv Shankar Kumar, the learned A.P.P. has submitted the objection at the Bar.
Let the same be kept on record.

Heard Mr. Arvind Kumar Choudhary, the learned counsel for the appellant and Mr. Shiv Shankar Kumar, the learned A.P.P. assisted by Mr. Onkar Nath Tiwary, the learned counsel appearing for the informant.
This application has been preferred by the appellant for grant of bail during the pendency of this appeal.

The appellant has been convicted for the offences under sections 376(1) and 366 of the Indian Penal Code and has been sentenced to RI for 14 years along with a fine of Rs.10,000/- for the offence under section 376(1) of the Indian Penal Code.
It has been alleged that the daughter of the informant was enticed away by the appellant with the assistance of several named accused persons.

Submission has been advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant that in the 164 Cr.P.C.
statement

the victim has categorically stated that she had accompanied the appellant voluntarily to various places and had also returned back to SP office along with the appellant from where they were apprehended by the police.

It has been submitted that however in course of trial the victim who has been examined as PW-3 has given a different version to the effect that she was forced to give such 164 Cr.P.C. statement under threat from the appellant.

sentences.text: The learned A.P.P. as well as the learned counsel appearing for the informant have opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant.

It appears from the evidence of the victim that she was taken from Deoghar to Dumka and thereafter to Howrah and thereafter they returned back to SP office, Deoghar and during all this period the victim had never raised any hue and cry.
In fact, the love affair between the victim and the appellant seems to be apparent in the 164 Cr.P.C. statement of the victim.
On consideration of the aforesaid facts, we are inclined to admit the appellant on bail.

Accordingly,
during the pendency of this appeal, the appellant is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Rs. Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Special Judge, POCSO at Deoghar in Sarwan PS Case No. 117 of 2021,
corresponding to Special POCSO Case No. 02 of 2022.
I.A. stands disposed of.

(RONGON MUKHOPADHYAY, J.)
S.B. (AMBUJ NATH, J.)
